claim_as_currently_worded: Reported KS p values for 7 to 14 cells per group are below the smallest value cells could give (audit_p.md C11, K7 'can be firmer')
where_worded: pv_inv15_20261107/verify/audit_p.md C11 and section 5; output/README.md (Added after the audit)
what_the_paper_declares: Legends of Fig. 4 give p values with "KS test" and the cell and animal N's; the model 'one value per cell' is not declared by the authors.
reconstructable_from_aggregate_statistic: partly, arithmetic on the declared N's only. Exact smallest two-sided p of a two-sample KS test with n and m single values is 2/C(n+m,n). With cells as units: sIPSC (14 v 9: floor 2.5e-6; 7 v 9: 1.8e-4): all six reported values fall below the floor (6 of 6) (smallest 9.2e-135); mEPSC amplitude WT-KO 4.99e-7 and HT-KO 1.33e-6 (10 v 10: floor 1.1e-5) fall below, WT-HT 1.98e-4 and all three mEPSC frequency values do not; sEPSC amplitude WT-KO 3.5e-23 (14 v 17: floor 7.5e-9) and HT-KO 5.5e-26 (17 v 17: floor 8.6e-10) fall below, CTL-KO 1.5e-5 (18 v 17: floor 4.4e-10) and all sEPSC frequency values do not. Without the raw events or cell-level values no test can be reconstructed.
restated_claim: If cells were the units, 10 of the 18 reported KS values (all six sIPSC, two mEPSC amplitude, two sEPSC amplitude) could not have been obtained, because each lies below the smallest p the exact two-sample KS test can return for the declared N's; the other 8 are compatible with cells. If events were the units, no inconsistency arises, but the inference is then about events pooled over few animals. The paper declares neither model, so no internal contradiction of the paper is asserted. Without the raw events or cell-level values the tests cannot be reconstructed, and in their absence the KS values describe event distributions and carry no animal-level inference.
effect_on_INV15_INV18: INV-15: the sentence 'the p values imply events as units' becomes 'the p values are compatible with events as units and incompatible with one value per cell; the paper does not declare the unit'. No contradiction of the paper is claimed. INV-18: not used.

claim_as_currently_worded: Independence: events within cells within animals
where_worded: (new framing; pv_inv15 README states 'events were the unit' as arithmetic)
what_the_paper_declares: Methods 6.7: "Sample size represents at least the minimum number of samples needed to establish significance." No mixed model, no animal-level test and no correction for clustering is named. Fig. 4E and G legends: "Right graph shows total mean ± standard error of sEPSCs for all animals."
reconstructable_from_aggregate_statistic: partly. Table 1 N's give 5/6/15 pyramidal and 4/5 interneuron animals, enough to say what the independent replication is; whether any test was run on animal-level summaries is not stated (the right-hand graphs of Fig. 4E and G are described as 'for all animals').
restated_claim: Events within a cell, and cells within an animal, are not independent observations. A test that treats them as independent can return very small p values from a small number of animals; this is a limit on what the p values support, not an error attributed to the authors. Animal-level statistics are not reported for sIPSC, sEPSC or mEPSC amplitude; for sag (Fig. 6B legend: 'average ± SEM for all animals tested') the unit of the plot and its t-test may be the animal, which the legend does not settle [corrected after the independent audit].
effect_on_INV15_INV18: INV-15 and INV-18: add the sentence 'animals, not cells or events, are the replicates; the paper gives no animal-level statistics', which both rows already ask of the future experiment. Do not word it as a flaw of the authors.

claim_as_currently_worded: Sag at -200 pA read as 'a larger HCN contribution'; absolute sag grows even if HCN density is unchanged (Y04)
what_the_paper_declares: Methods 6.6: "The sag voltage was measured by subtracting the most negative membrane deflection from its return to steady state"; "a hyperpolarizing pulse of -200pA". Table 1: "Sag (at −200 pA)". The step is fixed in current for every cell; no protocol at a matched membrane potential is described.
reconstructable_from_aggregate_statistic: partly. The fixed-current design is declared; with a fixed current the deflection scales with each cell's input resistance, so the table compares cells driven to different potentials. A comparison at matched membrane potential does not exist in the paper and cannot be built from means.
restated_claim: (i) Fixed current step: this is what the paper did; groups with higher input resistance are driven further, so absolute sag at -200 pA is not a measure of Ih density. (ii) Matched membrane potential: not done; it is the comparison that would isolate a channel difference (experiment X1 of the HCN package). Ohm's law gives the first-order steady deflection (resistance times current) only; sag is non-linear and voltage-dependent (Ih activation, Kir and other K+ conductances, capacitance and time course, T-type recovery), so Y04's 'even if HCN density is unchanged' holds as a possibility, not as an estimate of how much of the sag rise is passive.
effect_on_INV15_INV18: INV-18: keep the matched-potential requirement (already present: 'a current-clamp step that matches the resting potential'; add 'and the peak potential'). HCN package Y04 stays with the word 'possibly'.

claim_as_currently_worded: Estimated steady deflection about 20.6, 28.7, 28.6 mV; peak potential about -101, -106, -105 mV; sag fraction 5.4, 6.6, 8.2 percent (Y05 to Y07)
where_worded: hcn_20261107/output/physiology.tsv Y05, Y06, Y07; HCN README INFERENZA 1 and 'Added after the audit'; verify/audit_c.md H1
what_the_paper_declares: Methods 6.6: "Input resistance was measured by the slope of the computed I-V plot." The current range of the slope is not stated; the sag and the deflection are not reported per cell.
reconstructable_from_aggregate_statistic: no for any new number; the three rows are products of group means (resistance times 0.2 nA; resting potential minus deflection minus sag). They are linear, assume the I-V slope equals the steady response at -200 pA, treat ratios of means as means of ratios, and carry no variance. Where Ih or Kir is active the slope near rest may overestimate the steady deflection at -200 pA, so the deflections are upper-end illustrations.
restated_claim: Y05 to Y07 are linear illustrations of scale, not estimates: they show that the same current drives high-resistance cells several mV further, not by how much, nor what fraction of the sag is passive (audit: about one third in KO and one half in HT with the sag fraction held fixed; the fraction rise is about 1.6 standard errors in KO and about 0.7 in HT, so it is not shown for HT [corrected after the independent audit]). The README sentence 'does not need extra HCN' should read 'need not require extra HCN; the linear part accounts for only a share; the non-linear share is undetermined'.
effect_on_INV15_INV18: INV-18: nothing in the row relies on Y05 to Y07 numbers; keep branch D. HCN package: soften Answer first ('does not need extra HCN') and INFERENZA 1 ('Sag as a fraction still rises') to 'not shown to differ'; Y05, Y06 labelled 'linear illustration, upper end'.

claim_as_currently_worded: Authors: 'the hyperpolarization activated potassium current was elevated, as evidenced by a larger hyperpolarization'; Discussion heading 'increased sag current'
where_worded: hcn_20261107/output/evidence.tsv E01 to E10 (as sources); README DATO 2; investigations_it20.tsv INV-18 (sag graded with gene dose)
what_the_paper_declares: Results 2.6: "the hyperpolarization activated potassium current was elevated, as evidenced by a larger hyperpolarization in response to a negative current injection". Discussion 3.5, first sentence of the paragraph (not a heading): "Pyramidal neurons of Wwox S-KO mice show increased sag current, stronger post-inhibitory rebound, depolarized neuronal membrane potential". No voltage-clamp Ih record and no blocker in the paper.
reconstructable_from_aggregate_statistic: not applicable (a wording matter). The authors' evidence for an elevated current is the larger deflection to the same step, which is the quantity that input resistance already changes.
restated_claim: Statements about Ih in this paper rest on a current-clamp sag at a fixed current. They are compatible with a larger Ih, with a larger passive deflection recruiting the same Ih, with changed K+ conductances, with smaller cells, or with T-type contributions to rebound; none of the four is separated by the data. Network-activity consequences are a fifth, separate question (bursting is a slice-level finding: 36 of 42 KO slices from 24 animals, 4 of 23 HT slices from 14 animals, 0 of 11 WT slices from 7 animals).
effect_on_INV15_INV18: INV-18: wording 'graded sag' stays as a table fact; where the row calls the sag 'Ih' or implies HCN, it should say 'sag at a fixed current'. The row already carries the requirement that sag be shown to be Ih by blocker sensitivity.
